deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page studies the plane quartic (p=3): bitangent root functions sqrt(x), sqrt(xi), ... labelled by odd 3-digit characteristics, and relations such as sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0. The next page counts even and odd theta characteristics (alpha_p, beta_p). This page tries to carry the quartic picture over to general genus p. It does this by working on the plane curve of degree 2p-2 cut out by ratios of three differentials of the first kind, i.e. a plane projection of the canonical curve. It ends with theta-quotient formulas built from determinants.

(A) Characteristic tables, top of page. Two tables are headed (000/010) and (000/001). Each column holds two characteristics, read as A=(row1/row2) and B=(row3/row4).
- Under (000/001), most legible columns give pairs of odd characteristics summing to the header, e.g. (100/100)+(100/101), (100/110)+(100/111), (110/100)+(110/101), (110/010)+(110/011), (010/110)+(010/111).
- So these are Steiner-complex-type lists: the 6 pairs of odd characteristics with a fixed sum (p=3).
- The labels are 100/100=x, 100/110=z, 100/101=y, 100/111=t. All four are odd: the parity sum g.h equals 1 for each.
- They satisfy x+z = y+t = (000/010), x+y = z+t = (000/001), y+z = x+t = (000/011), and x+y+z+t = 0. This is a syzygetic tetrad. These three pairings reappear at the bottom of the page as sqrt(xz) with sqrt(yt), sqrt(xy) with sqrt(zt), and sqrt(yz) with sqrt(xt).
- Some columns are mis-transcribed (or slips); see corrections.

(B) The curve. F(x,y,z) is homogeneous of degree n=2p-2. Written as a_0 y^(2p-2)+a_1 y^(2p-3)+...+a_(2p-2)=0, y has 2p-2 values (becoming infinite where a_0=0). F'(y) is infinite of order 2p-3 when x is infinite. The differentials of the first kind are phi_(2p-5)(x,y,z) dx/F'(y), with phi of degree n-3 = 2p-5.

(C) Number of branch points and double points.
- Plücker count (my reading): w = n(n-1)-2r = (2p-3)(2p-2)-2r.
- Riemann–Hurwitz with 2p-2 sheets: w = 2(2p-2)+2(p-1) = 6p-6. This is the corrected '=6p-6' in the image.
- Equating gives r = 2(p-1)(p-3) = 2(p-2)^2-2 = 2p^2-8p+6. This is also (2p-3)(2p-4)/2 - p, the number of nodes of a nodal plane model of degree 2p-2 and genus p. It is the generic plane projection of the canonical curve.

(D) Adjoint counts.
- (i) phi_(2p-5): it has (2p-4)(2p-3)/2 = (p-2)(2p-3) coefficients. Requiring phi=0 at the r double points leaves (p-2)(2p-3)-2(p-1)(p-3) = p free coefficients. These are the p integrals of the first kind.
- (ii) f = phi_(2p-6), adjoint of degree n-4: it has (2p-5)(2p-4)/2 = (p-2)(2p-5) = 2(p-2)^2-(p-4)-2 = r-(p-4) coefficients. Riemann asserts that of the r conditions f=0 at the double points, p-4 follow from the others.
  - In modern terms (mine): the lines cut the canonical class H=K. Since K = (n-3)H - Delta, the adjoint divisor satisfies Delta ~ (n-4)H.
  - Hence there is exactly one adjoint curve of degree 2p-6 (up to a constant), cutting out nothing beyond the nodes.
- (iii) phi_(2p-4): (p-1)(2p-3) coefficients, 3p-3 free, i.e. h^0(2K) = 3(p-1).
- (iv) phi_(2p-3): (p-1)(2p-1) coefficients, 5(p-1) free.
- (v) phi_(2p-2): p(2p-1) coefficients, 7(p-1) free, after subtracting the multiple F itself.
- (vi) General case, degree 2p-3+m: [(2p-2+m)(2p-1+m) - m(m+1)]/2 - 2(p-1)(p-3). Here m(m+1)/2 counts the multiples F*g with deg g = m-1. The result simplifies via (2m+1)(p-1)+2(p-1)^2-2(p-1)(p-3) to (2m+5)(p-1), i.e. h^0((m+3)K).

(E) Forms of weight m.
- phi_(2p-5)/phi_(2p-6) vanishes at 2p-2 points: a canonical divisor.
- phi_(2p-6+m)/phi_(2p-6) vanishes at 2m(p-1) points, the degree of mK.
- For m>1 such ratios have (2m-1)(p-1) arbitrary coefficients. This is Riemann–Roch for h^0(mK). The case m=2 gives the 3p-3 count.

(F) Theta quotients via determinants.
- psi denotes a phi_(2p-4) vanishing where x=0 (my reading: simply, at the p-1 contact points of the 'contact form' x). chi denotes the analogous form for y. Each family has 2p-2 independent members: h^0(2K-D_x) = 3p-3-(p-1).
- Formula: Sum±psi^1(P_1)...psi^(2p-2)(P_(2p-2)) / Sum±chi^1(P_1)...chi^(2p-2)(P_(2p-2)) * sqrt(y_1...y_(2p-2)/(x_1...x_(2p-2))) = A * theta(Sum_j u(P_j)+half period with characteristic (g,h)) / theta(Sum_j u(P_j)+half period with characteristic (g',h')).
- Consistency check (mine): psi/sqrt(x) is a section of 2K - eta_x, of degree 3p-3. So in each P_j the determinant has 2p-3 zeros at the other P's plus p further zeros, matching the p zeros of a theta function. The formula is structurally sound.
- He then splits the points into two groups of p-1. He uses (p-1)-rowed determinants of psi's attached to sqrt(xz) and chi's attached to sqrt(yz), obtaining B*theta/theta.
- The product of the two half-quotients equals B^2 under a condition on Sum_1^(2p-2) of the arguments, related to the points x=0, y=0.

(G) Last lines. He pairs root functions as in the tetrad: sqrt(xz) ... sqrt(yt), sqrt(xy) ... sqrt(zt), sqrt(yz) . sqrt(xt). He forms products of quotients sqrt(xz) Sum±(p-2 rows, x=0)/(sqrt(xt) Sum±...) times sqrt(yt) Sum±(y=0)/(sqrt(yz) Sum±...). This prepares the next page's sqrt(yz/(xt)) = c_(2p-4)/c_(2p-4): a quotient of two root functions with characteristics in the same Steiner pairing is a ratio of two quadratic-differential adjoints. This generalizes the quartic relation sqrt(xyzt) = conic.
errors: The statement that p-4 of the r node conditions on f=phi_(2p-6) are consequences of the others gives, with (p-2)(2p-5) = r-(p-4) coefficients, zero free coefficients, i.e. only f=0. A unique nonzero adjoint of degree 2p-6 (up to scalar) needs p-3 dependent conditions. Either a slip by one, or Riemann is counting conditions on coefficient ratios.

The general formula (2m+5)(p-1) (with the subtraction m(m+1)/2) is valid only for m >= -1. For m=-2 (degree 2p-5) it gives p-1 instead of p, because there are no multiples of F to subtract. Riemann uses it only for m >= -1, so this is harmless.
The w lines contain crossed-out intermediate values. The final w = 6p-6 is correct; the transcription's '4p-2' is wrong.

The theta-quotient formulas are stated without proof. The constants A and B, the exact characteristics (g,h), (g',h') and the condition under which the product equals B^2 are not specified. These are plausible but unverified on the page.

results.what: Plane model of degree 2p-2 given by ratios of three differentials of the first kind (projected canonical curve), with 2(p-1)(p-3) double points, derived from branch-point counts (Plücker vs Riemann–Hurwitz).
results.modern_name: Canonical curve / its generic plane projection; genus formula for nodal plane curves
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1857) for the phi-ratios; Brill–Noether (1874), Noether, Weber for systematic treatment

results.what: Counts of adjoint curves: p adjoints of degree 2p-5; a unique adjoint of degree 2p-6; (2m+5)(p-1) free coefficients for degree 2p-3+m modulo F.
results.modern_name: Brill–Noether adjoint theory; Riemann–Roch h^0(mK) = (2m-1)(p-1), including 3p-3 quadratic differentials

results.what: Syzygetic tetrad x,y,z,t of odd characteristics (p=3 labels) and Steiner-complex tables of pairs of odd characteristics with fixed sum.
results.modern_name: Steiner complexes / syzygetic tetrads of theta characteristics
results.usually_credited_to: Steiner, Hesse (1855) for bitangents; Riemann's own quartic notes; Weber 1876; Frobenius

results.what: Quotient of determinants of quadratic-differential adjoints vanishing at contact points, evaluated at 2p-2 points and multiplied by sqrt(prod y_j/prod x_j), expressed as a quotient of theta functions with half-period characteristics. Also a (p-1)-point splitting.
results.modern_name: Determinantal theta-function identities (Frobenius–Stickelberger / Fay-type formulas; Klein's and Schottky's determinant formulas)
results.usually_credited_to: Klein (1886-88), Schottky, Noether (1880s); modern form Fay (1973)

deep.surprise_reason: The adjoint counts and canonical-model node count are routine, essentially Riemann's own 1857 framework. More notable is an unpublished attempt to generalize the p=3 bitangent/Steiner-complex picture to arbitrary p. It writes theta quotients as quotients of determinants of quadratic differentials vanishing at contact points, anticipating determinant formulas usually associated with Klein, Schottky, Noether and later Fay. It remains sketchy (constants and characteristics unspecified), so it is a notable but not major unpublished detail.

checkable.asserts: Node count r=2(p-1)(p-3) gives genus p for degree 2p-2 (expect 0)
Adjoints of degree 2p-5 have p free coefficients (expect 0)
Coefficient count of degree 2p-6 forms equals r-(p-4) (expect 0)
With p-3 dependent conditions there is exactly 1 free coefficient for the degree-(2p-6) adjoint (expect 0)
General count for degree 2p-3+m modulo multiples of F equals (2m+5)(p-1) (expect 0)
x,y,z,t odd (parities [1,1,1,1]); x+z=y+t=(000/010), x+y=z+t=(000/001), y+z=x+t=(000/011): a syzygetic tetrad matching the page's pairings

transcription_corrections: 'w=2p+2(p-1) = 4p-2 [?]' should read 'w = 2n+2(p-1)' with n=2p-2 sheets (the page shows a variant crossed and overwritten); the final value in the image is '= 6p-6'.

'Wendepunkte' (inflection points) is mathematically wrong: the r points are double points of the curve. The word is probably 'Werthsysteme(n)' (Riemann's term for points), referring to the double points; likewise in 'für 2p-2 ...' and 'für 2m(p-1) ...'.
'discriminirtes' is doubtful; the sense is 'an (arbitrary/such) phi_(2p-4) which vanishes where x=0'.
'zu Fernach mit sqrt(xz) gefügt' is doubtful; the sense is 'belonging to (forms associated with) sqrt(xz)'.
'Rinnen' is doubtful; probably 'Summen' or similar, i.e. a condition on the sum of the 2p-2 arguments relative to the points x=0, y=0.

In the characteristic tables, columns should read as pairs A=(row1/row2), B=(row3/row4) with A+B equal to the header. Several transcribed columns (e.g. second table column 4 '100,010,010,011', first table columns 2 and 4) are inconsistent with this and are probably misread.
'001/000 = z' duplicates the label z; probably a different letter or characteristic.
